messages:
Anya: OKR planning alert — we need a concrete procurement + region expansion plan for infra capacity over the next 12 months. Customers keep asking for APAC low-latency zones and Dedicated capacity. Can we outline feasible waves given vendor lead times and our cost OKR?
Devon: +1. Vendor lead times we've been quoted are still long (12–20 weeks for H100 orders). We should consider a hybrid approach: reserved commits for baseline + spot/short-term rentals for burst.
Sam: Quick sketch of numbers (very rough):
```
OptionA: Reserve 200 H100 (NA/EU) -> lead 16w -> baseline throughput ~1.2M tokens/s
OptionB: Reserve 80 H100 + 120 L4 spot -> mixed latency/cost -> lead 12w for H100
OptionC: 40 H100 pilot APAC (rental) -> immediate (2–4w) -> test <50ms P99 for region
```
Devon: That looks sensible. For APAC my priority is: pilot small (rental) to validate routing + KV cache benefits before committing to long lead-time buys.
Leila: Also flagging infra constraints: eu-west2 PDUs have ~120kW spare, we can't fit large waves there without new power installs (8–12w). ap-sg racks are thin on capacity; need colo leadtime check. 
Priya: From product/enterprise: customers asking for region pinning + 99.95% SLO. They're willing to pay a premium for Dedicated in APAC. For PLG users we can route to hosted NA with slightly higher latency. 
Anya: OK so tradeoffs: cost OKR wants -18% cost per 1M tokens, ops wants latency SLOs for enterprise in APAC. Proposal: Wave0 (pilot): 12 H100 rental APAC + 16 L4 for inference-caching tests. Wave1 (reserve): commit 120 H100 across NA/EU for baseline Q1. Wave2 (top-up): spot pools + cloud rentals for seasonal peaks.
Devon: Wave timelines: Wave0 deploy by end of Q3 (rental contract 2–4w), Wave1 orders placed by Oct (16w lead), Wave2 ongoing. Need vendor holdbacks for staggered delivery.
Sam: I'll attach the cost delta calc in the procurement tracker but quick numbers: reserves reduce per-token cost ~22% vs pure spot, but upfront commitment impacts cash. Rentals are +40% cost but allow fast validation.
Leila: Operational ask — we need a simple auto-fallback policy: if local queue depth > X or tail latency > Y ms, route to fallback pool (NA/EU). Can we define X/Y? Suggest X=200 reqs in queue OR P95>120ms -> fallback.
Priya: Product accepts fallback behavior for non-enterprise. For enterprise accounts we must try local pools first and only fallback with explicit customer permission unless outage.
Anya: Draft launch criteria for APAC Dedicated: (1) Pilot validates P99<60ms for production mix, (2) KV cache hit rate >= 25% on canonical prompts, (3) cost per 1M tokens <= target w/ reserved mix OR documented customer premium.
Sam: Action items: 1) Devon to confirm vendor rental contacts + ETA. 2) Leila to validate rack power & network ports for ap-sg colo. 3) Finance to model reserve vs rental cash flow (Priya loop in). 4) Infra to draft auto-fallback SLO config.
Devon: I've pinged vendor contact (will DM pricing). Also proposing a small experiment: try 4 H100 + 8 L4 in APAC under canary traffic for 2 weeks to measure real-world latency and KV cache benefits.
ops-bot: New RFC created: https://redwood.internal/rfc/infra-capacity-2027-draft (status: draft)
Anya: Good. Can everyone drop a one-line risk we should call out in the RFC by EOD? I'll own collating. :thumbsup:
Priya: Risk — commitment size too large before validating customer routing patterns (mitigation: staged purchases + rentals).
Leila: Risk — colo power/network delays (mitigation: early site survey + PDU reservations).
Sam: Risk — finance approval delay (mitigation: bridge rental budget).
Devon: Risk — vendor allocation shortfalls (mitigation: multiple vendors + staggered delivery).
Anya: Thanks — I'll assemble and update the RFC. Meeting to finalize procurement wave decisions tomorrow 10:00am PT.
Leila: I'll bring rack diagrams and PDU numbers.
Sam: I'll push the procurement spreadsheet link in the RFC and tag finance.
Devon: I'll prepare a vendor ordinal (preferred -> backup) + expected lead windows.
Priya: I'll prepare a short customer SLA matrix to map to capacity tiers.
